reason: This passage depicts Isaac (the patriarch/elder with authority) and Esau (the firstborn heir) in an unfavorable light. Isaac is portrayed as physically weak (blind), gullible, and easily deceived by Jacob and Rebekah's scheme—he cannot distinguish between his own sons and is manipulated into giving the superior blessing to the younger son. Esau, as the firstborn, is similarly undermined and outmaneuvered, receiving only an inferior blessing ('by the sword you shall live, and your brother you shall serve'). The narrative presents the elite figures of authority as foolish and vulnerable to trickery, while the younger Jacob successfully exploits their weaknesses, suggesting an unfavorable portrayal of those with power and status in this family hierarchy.
